themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization the models call the output non-deterministic with no stable baseline; on cross-channel incrementality they say the platform reacts to the test; on identity resolution they propose recruiting a consenting panel as a truth set; on B2B buying-group signal loss and content governance they note reviewers and outcomes give no reliable answer key.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models route every write through a proxy or gateway with hard spend and audience caps; on downstream consent they funnel every data exit through a single checkpoint; on journey orchestration they make every channel check one shared contact log before sending.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models describe ad platforms and trained models as black boxes with no person-level proof of removal; on incrementality they note platforms control both the treatment and the evidence; on ad supply integrity they say verification costs more per impression than faking it.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models offer fast declared-agent lanes and perks because agents profit by looking human; on journey orchestration they say channel owners are paid to keep sending; on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions a political settlement; on ad supply integrity they say the open web profits from fake volume.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance the models build approved-claim registries and constrain what can be generated because implied meaning across image, tone and audience resists automated checks; on the semantic context layer they argue for forced disclosure of which definition was used rather than one global definition.
